Messages.Author: witness1
Messages.Body:
On Sep 18, 11:27 am, "Orpheus" <orpheus...@free.fr> wrote:
> At what exact time is a bleed considered succesful ?

After blocks are declined and each methuselah passes on playing
further effects.

> Can it still be boosted through cards that require the bleed to be succesful
> ?

At this point, it can *only* be boosted by cards that require a
successful bleed.

> How would Zygodat"s special interfere with Trochomancy ?

Trochomancy has to be played before the bleed resolves. Zygodat's
special can only be used after the bleed resolves successfully (by
card text).
Only by specific card text (Zygodat, Dis Pater, Major Boon) can you
play an effect after the bleed resolves successfully.

witness1

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
witness1 wrote:
> On Sep 18, 11:27 am, "Orpheus" <orpheus...@free.fr> wrote:
>> At what exact time is a bleed considered succesful ?
>
> After blocks are declined and each methuselah passes on playing
> further effects.

Yes.
That is, when it reaches resolution successfully (unblocked) and the bleed
amount is for 1 or more.

>> Can it still be boosted through cards that require the bleed to be succesful
>> ?
>
> At this point, it can *only* be boosted by cards that require a
> successful bleed.

Yes. In-play Spying Mission, for example, is handled at this time.

>> How would Zygodat"s special interfere with Trochomancy ?
>
> Trochomancy has to be played before the bleed resolves. Zygodat's
> special can only be used after the bleed resolves successfully (by
> card text).
> Only by specific card text (Zygodat, Dis Pater, Major Boon) can you
> play an effect after the bleed resolves successfully.

Correct. Trochomancy has the same timing as any other standard bleed modifier,
like Conditioning.
